title: No phones at school in England!
lead: The government says schools in England should be phone-free. How do the schools do it?
body: In England, the government wants all schools to be "phone-free". Pupils shouldn't use their mobile phones during lessons, between lessons, at break or at lunch.
Each school chooses how to do it. Some schools collect the phones in the morning. Others ask pupils to put them in a locker, or in a pouch: a small bag that stays closed until the end of the day.
In West Norfolk, in the east of England, some secondary schools already had a phone-free policy. Pupils can bring their phone to school, but they can't use it before they leave.
Why? The idea is to have fewer distractions in class, to help pupils concentrate, and to encourage them to talk to each other.
